test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 27 Dec, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: The marked price of an item was Rs. 2,000, but the shopkeeper offered successive discounts of 20% and 15% on its sale. How much did he finally sell the item for?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net discount % = a + b − (a × b ÷ 100)

Net discount = 20 + 15 − (20 × 15 ÷ 100) = 35 − 3 = 32%

Selling Price (SP) = Marked Price (MP) × (100 − Net Discount%) ÷ 100

SP = 2000 × (100 − 32) ÷ 100 = 2000 × 68 ÷ 100 = 20 × 68 = 1360

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 1360.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Marked Price (MP)** = Rs. 2000, **First Discount (d₁)** = 20%, **Second Discount (d₂)** = 15%.

**Formulas:** SP = MP × (100 − d₁)/100 × (100 − d₂)/100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/215c4cd7717cfca89c2ad7acb67c8aecd93a1c55ec84ac3730ce71194cd1868c.png] 

⇒ Price after 1st discount = 2000 × (80/100) = Rs. 1600

⇒ Price after 2ⁿd discount (Final SP) = 1600 × (85/100)

⇒ Final SP = 16 × 85 = Rs. 1360

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 1360.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discounts

When two or more discounts are applied one after another on the reduced price, they are called **successive discounts**. The total effective discount is always less than the sum of individual discount percentages.

Marked Price & Selling Price

**Marked Price (MP)** is the price printed on the label. **Selling Price (SP)** is the actual price after subtracting the **Discount** from the MP. SP = MP − Discount.</p
